PullRequest.Title: Chat resources: let the agent choose how the chat shows what it records
PullRequest.Body:
Part of #345427.

Chat resources ([#345428](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/pull/345428), merged) let the user pin a file that the chat's agent recorded into a pill of its own and show it above the chat input. Often the agent knows best what to show: a status or plan file it keeps updating is worth having above the input right away. This PR lets the agent ask for that when it records the file.

![An agent records status.md with mode aboveInput; the chat pins it and shows it above the input](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/d70a2c54-c751-4b9f-b965-63d1572d4d47)

## How it works

`add_artifact_or_reference` gets an optional `mode` per file:

```json
{ "type": "file", "label": "Bug #1234 status", "isArtifact": true, "uri": "file:///repo/status.md", "mode": "aboveInput" }
```

- `pinned`: the chat pins the file into a pill of its own, as the pin in the Artifacts list does.
- `aboveInput`: the chat also checks **Show Above Chat Input** for it and shows it.
- Without `mode`, the file is only listed, as before.

The mode is stored with the artifact. Each chat applies a request **once**, doing what the user would do, and remembers that it did (in workspace storage, per chat). So the user's later changes stick: unpinning or hiding the file stays that way until the agent records the file again with another mode. This keeps the shared pin state as it is; it has no "default" layer.

## Gating

- The agent host offers `mode` only while `chat.resources.enabled` is on. The setting is mirrored to the host as the root config key `chatResources`. A `mode` sent while it is off is ignored.
- With the setting off (the default), the tool schema, the prompt baselines and the chat's behavior are unchanged.

## Validation

- Unit tests: parsing and storing `mode`; offering it only with the setting on, through the agent service; the workbench pinning and showing a requested file once, keeping the user's change, and applying a new request.
- End to end in Code OSS with a Copilot CLI chat: the agent wrote `status.md` and recorded it with `mode: "aboveInput"`; the chat pinned it and showed it above the input without any click (screenshot above).

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: Repository-wide search proves the new key has only read/store sites and no cleanup, and the control call path proves full-history parsing. The time needed to become noticeable varies with session/resource churn.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Persisted JSON bytes and reconstructed JavaScript objects for historical session/resource request entries
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The stored object grows with every session that ever receives a request and every requested resource in that session (S × R), independent of how many sessions or artifacts still exist. Every control request pass parses and reconstructs the complete history, and each new request serializes it again.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Long-lived workspaces retain increasing storage and incur rising renderer CPU/GC and chat-opening latency as obsolete request history accumulates.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR there was no applied-request history. Rendering a chat therefore did not parse or retain a workspace-wide map of historical agent mode requests.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The PR stores all applied request tokens under one workspace key and `_readAppliedRequests` rebuilds every session's nested object, but no removal path exists when an artifact or session is removed.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 290 serializes `{ ...all, [chat]: applied }`, retaining every prior chat/session entry. The adjacent newly added reader enumerates all stored chats, while the diff adds no lifecycle cleanup.
Findings.Title: Prune applied requests with their session lifecycle
Findings.Impact: Users who create/delete many agent sessions or rotate recorded status files accumulate entries forever; opening or updating any later chat synchronously processes all obsolete entries.
Findings.Evidence: The only references to `chat.resources.appliedRequests` are the new store at line 290 and full parser `_readAppliedRequests`; there is no delete/prune call. `_applyRequests` starts by reading the whole map on its renderer autorun, and its store spreads all historical sessions back into JSON. Artifact and agent-session removal paths exist elsewhere but do not touch this key.
Findings.Recommendation: Tie applied tokens to artifact/session removal and delete empty nested maps, or store them in lifecycle-owned session metadata with bounded retention; also avoid materializing unrelated sessions when applying requests for the current session.

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed renderer call path, unbounded batch input, and per-item full-map persistence are directly visible. Exact user batch sizes and milliseconds vary, which affects severity but not the mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: Synchronous JSON parsing/serialization and workspace/profile storage operations on the renderer thread
Findings.PerformanceScaling: For R unique existing recorded resources carrying a new request, the loop invokes one pin persistence and one opens-in-chat persistence per resource. Each pin call reparses the entire profile pin map twice and rewrites it, while each opens-in-chat call reparses and rewrites its workspace map, so a batch performs O(R) storage mutations and O(R²) aggregate copying as the maps grow.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: Large artifact batches can block the renderer while the chat input updates, causing delayed pill rendering and dropped frames.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Before this PR, publishing a batch of artifacts did not automatically pin resources or persist per-resource chat display choices; those writes occurred only one at a time in response to explicit user actions.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: The new autorun sends all requested resources through _applyRequests, whose loop calls _pin(resource) and then _setOpensInChat(...) separately for every unapplied request.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 279 places `_pin(resource)` in the per-resource loop; added line 283 then calls `_setOpensInChat` for the same item. This automatic batch path did not exist before the diff.
Findings.Title: Batch requested pins before persisting UI state
Findings.Impact: When an agent records a realistic batch of many files with mode set, the state publication synchronously triggers multiple whole-map reads, JSON transformations, writes, and storage events before the UI settles.
Findings.Evidence: _applyRequests iterates every effective resource request. _pin delegates to StandardChatInputPillSources.pin -> ChatInputPillPins.setPinned, which reads/parses the full pinned map twice and stores a full JSON replacement. _setOpensInChat similarly reads/parses and rewrites the complete workspace map. The artifact tool's items schema has no maximum, so one tool result can publish many unique file requests together; these operations are serial and synchronous in the renderer autorun.
Findings.Recommendation: Collect all newly applicable requests first, update pin and opens-in-chat maps in memory, and persist each backing storage key once per autorun/batch (with one notification/event), while marking requests applied only after the batched pin operation succeeds.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent/provider obtains artifact tool definitions with chat resources enabled
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The host reads the mirrored root configuration and materializes the server-tool catalogue before advertising/serializing it to the agent provider.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize/advertise server-tool definitions to the agent provider
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One catalogue per session advertisement/refresh; one changed definition of constant size
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same catalogue was advertised without the mode property.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before the provider sees the optional mode parameter, but the added bytes and allocations are constant and small.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of server-tool definitions; this change adds one constant-size schema property to one definition.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous local catalogue construction; provider advertisement remains under the existing host flow with no new burst or limiter requirement.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Definitions are dynamically regenerated so configuration changes are observed; no cache is added, but the extra map/spreads are constant over the small static definition list.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that no scaling performance regression is introduced on this scenario.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Provider refresh frequency varies, but the changed work is constant-size.
Scenarios.Verdict: No finding: the schema work is bounded and does not add a scaling boundary.

Scenarios.Scenario: Agent records or changes display modes for a batch of file artifacts
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Tool input parsing and session-sequenced mutation must complete durable artifact persistence before state publication and the tool returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Persist the merged session artifact list through ordered visible session state storage
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One persistence operation per changed tool batch, not per input
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Artifact additions/promotions already persisted the merged list once per changed batch.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before artifacts are published and the tool returns.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Associate recorded GitHub pull requests with the working folder
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One grouped association for unique GitHub pull-request URLs; file mode requests do not enter it
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same grouped association ran for recorded pull requests.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited for applicable pull-request batches, but unrelated to file modes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: B batch entries against A artifacts in the current chat, after artifact-value deduplication.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All mutations for a session are serialized by SequencerByKey; the batch is processed sequentially and persisted once after mutation.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No cache is involved; duplicate artifact values are coalesced by SessionArtifactCollection, and unchanged modes leave the collection identity unchanged so persistence is skipped.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High confidence that the host mode field itself does not add a reportable expensive boundary.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Artifact batches are unbounded by schema, but host-side mode handling adds only local field parsing/copying to the already-scaling collection mutation.
Scenarios.Verdict: No host-side finding: the durable boundary remains once per changed batch and mode handling does not increase its cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Published mode requests automatically pin files and optionally show them above the chat input
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A renderer autorun observes existing recorded resources, applies every unapplied request synchronously, mutates pin/open state, and only then lets dependent pill/resource rendering settle.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Observe existence of each unique recorded resource URI
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One cached observer per unique resource target
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Chat resources already observed each recorded file's existence.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: A resource request is applied only once existence resolves; this observation was already performed for recorded resources.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and rewrite the complete profile pinned-entry map
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Once per requested resource, with two full reads/parses per call
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only an individual user pin action invoked this persistence; publishing an artifact batch did not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously inside the renderer autorun before UI state settles.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Parse and rewrite the complete workspace opens-in-chat map
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Only individual user display actions invoked this persistence; artifact publication did not.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Runs synchronously in the same renderer loop.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Serialize and store applied request tokens
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One final full-map write per autorun that applies at least one request
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Adds another synchronous whole-history serialization before the pass completes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: R unique existing recorded resources carrying a new mode request after URI deduplication and file-existence filtering.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The loop is fully serial on the renderer thread; there is no coalescing of storage mutations across resources.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: A stored mode#revision token prevents repeating pin/open mutations for an identical request. Warm passes still parse and reconstruct the entire applied-request map; cold/new revisions execute all per-resource writes.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the serial loop and full-map storage implementations are directly traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical agents may request only one status file, while the tool permits arbitrarily large batches; exact frame impact depends on batch size and accumulated pin maps.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable missing-coalescing regression: batched requests fan out into synchronous per-resource persistence on the UI path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or update chats after long-term session and artifact churn in a workspace
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Creating the enabled ChatResourcesControl runs its request autorun, which synchronously loads, parses, enumerates, and reconstructs the workspace-wide applied-request history.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read and JSON-parse the workspace-wide applied-request map, then rebuild all nested objects
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-history parse per request autorun, regardless of current session size
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous on chat control creation/update and therefore delays renderer progress.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Rewrite all historical applied-request entries when the current session receives a new request
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One full-history serialization per changed pass
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No such retained history or rewrite existed.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Synchronous renderer work and growing persistent bytes.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total historical requested resources across all sessions ever processed in the workspace, including deleted sessions and removed artifacts.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single renderer-thread parse/rebuild per autorun; no lazy per-session read or background processing.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Tokens act as a positive cache for applied requests, but have no removal, expiry, cap, or session/artifact invalidation. Even warm hits require full-history parsing.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: Very high: the storage key has only read/store sites repository-wide and no lifecycle cleanup.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The number of sessions/resources needed for noticeable latency depends on workspace longevity and agent usage, but deletion workflows make stale history realistic.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable cache-lifecycle regression: obsolete entries are retained indefinitely and increase every later read/write cost.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all 14 changed files and all diff pages. Two diff-caused renderer regressions were submitted: uncoalesced per-resource persistence for batched mode requests, and unbounded applied-request history with full-map parsing/serialization. Host schema, parsing, collection mutation, and durable artifact persistence remain bounded or preserve prior boundary cardinality.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
